utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-PT, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. May I have the appearances. Prosecution, first.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Prosecution today, Mr. Dan Saxon, Ms. Melissa Pack, and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, and as usual we are coming together with our case manager, Ms. Ana Katalinic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. For the Defence. I see that Mr. Seselj, who is self-represented, is not present. Therefore, I would first like to know whether stand-by counsel is present. I see you are present, Mr. Hooper, accompanied by Mr. O'Shea and accompanied by ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HOOPER
utterances.text: Ms. Lea Kulinowski, who is our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Hooper. We've just established that Mr. Seselj is not present. Mr. Registrar, could you update, inform, the Chamber about the reasons of the absence of Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good morning. This morning I was informed by the acting Deputy Registrar, Mr. Robin Vincent, who was also reliably informed by the commanding officer of the Detention Unit, Mr. Tim McFadden, that Mr. Seselj does not want to attend today's proceedings. There has been no change in his circumstances in the fact that he continues to refuse food supplied by the Detention Unit, as well as medication. It's reported to me that his condition has grown weaker since last Friday, when he was observed. But apart from that, there has been no change to his day-to-day routine. He continues to drink water, and he has not been observed eating. Apart from that, he does not want to attend today's proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that information, Mr. Registrar. Before we continue, I'd first like to inform the parties about the new composition of the bench. Like Judge Hoepfel was assigned to the case pre-trial and then after the Secretary-General had approved his assignment to the Seselj case, it was then assigned to this case on the 31st of October. Similarly, Judge Stole has been assigned for the pre-trial stage of these proceedings by the President of this institution. I think it was last week, Friday, that the Secretary-General approved or, as a matter of fact, assigned Judge Stole also to the Seselj case, and this will be confirmed, I understand, before the start of the trial today by the President of this institution assigning Judge Stole to the Seselj Bench. So, therefore, this moment, he is still here on the basis of his assignment pre-trial, but will not start the trial until the President Pocar has signed an order noting his approval by the Secretary-General assigning Judge Stole to this case. The Chamber has not received any submissions in relation to the invitation to the accused to make submissions, which was filed and served on the accused in his own language on the 22nd of November, 2006. The Chamber is also not aware of any request for an extension of the deadlines set by that invitation. Since the accused is not present here, the Chamber cannot receive any oral submissions in respect of what has been raised in this invitation either. But whether or not the accused has responded to the invitation by the Chamber, the Chamber and I should now consider, in view of the accused's conduct, whether the accused's self-representation should be terminated and whether stand-by counsel, or counsel, I'd have to say, be imposed permanently. Unfortunately, the accused is not here to make any further submissions. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, does the Prosecution want to make any submissions in this respect, or would you prefer to leave this to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have made our position clear since a long time, that we think that counsel needs to be assigned to guarantee a proper trial here. We think -- and most recently also made a motion confirming this position. We think it should be permanent counsel; otherwise, we would have to face situations like the one we find ourselves in over and over again. That's actually all I need to add to all the arguments that we have been -- that have already been made in the filings. So we are -- we actually would also request that the permanent assignment of counsel and not temporary, as we had the last few days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, the Chamber will have to ignore for the time being the last motion because it has not been translated and therefore the accused is not aware of the content of that motion. So, therefore, any arguments set out in that motion where the accused had no opportunity to respond will, at this moment, not be considered by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, given that situation, I would like to add, then, just a very brief remark. In the motion that we filed and will now be ignored, the Prosecution has actually provided jurisprudence on the fact how hunger strikes and the like were considered in international law in this tribunal and in national law, and all the -- basically, these kinds of jurisprudence came to the result that hunger strike in the form as it is conducted here was considered to be obstructive. That's all I wanted to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hooper, since you're not activated at this moment as stand-by counsel, I'm not going to ask you at this moment to make any further submissions. That would need a decision, to invite you to take over, because the last time we decided for you to take over was just for the purposes of that Status Conference. If you'd like to respond to what I just said, you have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOOPER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. First of all, may we extend our congratulations to Judge Stole on his elevation to the Bench of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. Coming to the matter at hand, we would feel it not inappropriate for the Bench to invite a view from us as stand-by counsel as to the appropriate modalities for assignment of counsel. And I say no more at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hooper, the Chamber, but really very temporarily, decides to activate you to take over as counsel and to submit what you'd like to -- what you'd like to submit in relation to imposition of counsel. If you want to talk about modalities, fine, these kinds of matters, I think it may be clear enough to you that especially these kinds of matters, you are in a situation which is not an easy one. That means you are under a duty now to assist the Chamber in reaching decisions from a point of view most favourable to the accused. Please keep that in mind and make whatever submissions you'd like to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOOPER
utterances.text: Well, essentially, what I'd like to say is merely a reflection of a debate that's taken place between myself and my co-counsel this morning, and it really concerns this: It's the question of the modalities that concern us. I say "concern us." It's a matter that perhaps does merit being raised, and it's essentially to deal with -- deals with this: That so far, reference to Dr. -- by the Chamber, to Dr. Seselj, and I'm thinking here of the recent Status Conferences that have been held, has concern and been really directed by way of warning to him as to the temporary assignment of stand-by counsel to take over his case. And that in the Trial Chamber's written order, dated the 22nd of November, 2006, the Chamber has issued a warning in line with the Appeals Chamber decision, essentially, of the 20th of October of 2006, has issued a warning relating to the imposition of counsel, which is perhaps -- well, obviously a more specific and general imposition. And we merely raise, this morning, for your consideration, whether there should be, if that is the path that the Chamber feels should be followed, a further warning to the accused this morning, which he could respond to either this morning or tomorrow or such time as the Chamber would feel, in those circumstances, is appropriate. Those are all the matters that we have to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hooper. The Chamber will adjourn at this moment. We'll consider the present situation as far as representation by counsel or self-representation is concerned, whether temporarily or on a more permanent basis. We stand adjourned, and the parties are invited to remain stand-by. We'll take not more than -- at least the parties should take not more than 10 to 15 minutes. Of course, whether the Chamber has then reached a decision yet or not yet is still to be seen, but the parties should remain on stand-by from 25 minutes to 10.00. --- Break taken at 9.21 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now render an oral decision on the accused's self-representation, and the written reasons for this decision will follow soon, although, I'll give abbreviated reasons already, now. On the 22nd of November, 2006, following the accused's failure to appear at a Status Conference, the Chamber invited him, and I quote, "to make submissions regarding the recent conduct or any decision the Trial Chamber might take on the question of his legal representation," to be made no later than Friday, the 24th of November, 2006. The Chamber did not receive a response from the accused to its invitation. The accused has also failed to appear before this Chamber today to make any oral submissions on the matter. The Chamber, in accordance with the terms of its invitation to the accused, understands this as a waiver of his right to be heard on the matter. The Chamber has considered the conduct of the accused, in particular in the period since the Appeals Chamber's decision of the 20th of October, 2006. The Chamber has also considered the warnings that have been issued by the Chamber during the Status Conference of the 8th and the 22nd of November, 2006, and by the Appeals Chamber in the aforementioned decision. The Chamber has also considered that the accused persists in not taking food, requiring the Trial Chamber to reconsider some of its decisions. The Chamber also considered that the accused persists in being absent from the proceedings. The Chamber finds that the accused's self-representation in the course of the period since the 20th of October, 2006, has substantially obstructed the proper and expeditious conduct of the proceedings, and finds further, that permanent assignment of counsel to represent the accused in accordance with paragraph (I) of the Trial Chamber's order of the 25th of October, 2006, is at this point justified. Therefore, the Trial Chamber instructs stand-by counsel to permanently take over the conduct of the Defence from the accused, pursuant to paragraph 5(I) of the Trial Chamber's order of the 25th of October, 2006. The Trial Chamber orders that the accused's participation in the proceedings, henceforth, will be through counsel, unless, having heard from counsel, the Trial Chamber determines otherwise. The Trial Chamber further requests the Registry to appoint Mr. Van der Spoel as independent counsel, to take any necessary action in relation to an appeal against this decision, and to report to the Trial Chamber by tomorrow whether and how it has acted on this request. Mr. Hooper, I'll not address you any more as stand-by counsel, but I'll address you from now on as counsel, and we'll continue with the Pre-Trial Conference. I'd first like to go into private session, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before the Chamber decides on the matter, I'd like to hear from the parties whether any additional submissions are to be made. The last submissions were by the Prosecution, so perhaps, Mr. Hooper, I invite you to make any further submissions, the Chamber now having received an unredacted version giving the name, the place where the physician practices, and it is a signed, or at least there is what could be considered as a signature under this certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOOPER
utterances.text: We have no further submissions to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, may I then take it, or Mr. Saxon, that there are no further submissions to be made?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will now deliver its decision. The Chamber, having considered the submissions of the parties, has decided the following: Rule 71 bis provides that, and I quote, "at the request of either party, a Trial Chamber may, in the interests of justice, order that testimony be received via video-conference link." The Chamber notes that this Tribunal has found, on several occasions, that a party suffers no material disadvantage by examining a witness via videolink. An early decision to that effect was rendered in the case of The Prosecutor versus Delalic and others, on the 28th of May, 1997. In the present case, the Chamber considers that the physical condition of the witness, as indicated by the Prosecution, provides a strong ground for the witness to be allowed to give testimony via videolink. Therefore, it is in the interests of justice to hear Witness VS-053 via videolink. The testimony of Witness VS-053 is scheduled for the 8th of December, 2006. Before we continue, the Chamber went into private session because it could not anticipate what matters would be raised in this respect. The Chamber invites the parties to inform the Chamber on whether they consider that what we heard until now, in private session, could be made available to the public. Not necessarily to be done immediately but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Prosecution submits that what we have just heard in private session can be made available publicly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hooper.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOOPER
utterances.text: Yes, we agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll deal with that later. We'll continue now in private session in relation to the request for video-conference link for Witness VS-1141. At the Status Conference held on the 22nd of November, 2006, the Chamber also dealt with the Prosecution's motion filed on the 16th of November, 1996, to hear the testimony of Witness VS-1141 via videolink, in accordance with Rule 71 bis. The testimony of Witness VS-1141 has been scheduled for the 8th of December, 2006. The motion has not yet been translated and provided in translation to the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: During the Status Conference, temporarily-assigned counsel argued that the Prosecution did not sufficiently prove that the witness is unable to travel to The Hague to testify, and that a doctor should visit the witness to see if he's capable to come to the Tribunal and give evidence. At the Status Conference on the 22nd of November of this year, the Prosecution was invited to provide the Chamber and the Defence with an update on the reasons for the witness not being able to travel to The Hague to testify. As far as the Chamber is aware, the Prosecution has not filed any further submission regarding this issue. Therefore, Mr. Saxon, you're invited to provide an update on the matter, and the Chamber notes in this respect that it was stated on the Status Conference of the 22nd of November that an investigator and a lawyer were meeting the witness on that same day. Could you please update the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I misspoke slightly at the Status Conference of the 22nd of November. I thought that a lawyer and investigator were meeting with the witness on that day. That was incorrect. An investigator from our office and a lawyer met with a witness on the following day, Thursday, the 23rd of November. The investigator and the lawyer have since returned to The Hague, and the Prosecution is planning on submitting another declaration drafted by the investigator to the Chamber today regarding the most recent conversation and up-to-date information regarding this witness. And we would respectfully ask that the Chamber hold its decision on this matter in abeyance for one more day until the Chamber can read this most recent information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hooper, any response to this request?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOOPER
utterances.text: We'd invite the Prosecution to get a doctor to this witness and to provide and furnish the Court with medical evidence of his incapacity to travel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, we do not know what his submissions will be, whether this will report any earlier doctor visit. Mr. Saxon, is it ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: As of the 23rd of November, Your Honour, no, the witness has not seen a doctor, and the purpose of providing another declaration is for the investigator to explain, according to the witness, why not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, the Chamber will have to wait and see whether we could take a position, even without any medical certificates on the matter. But you asked for one more day, and that one more day is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. During the closed session, the Chamber dealt with two confidential motions. One of the issues discussed was testimony via video-conference link for Witness VS-053. That part of the transcript will be made available to the public. We'll now move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will deliver a decision on the expert witness Riedlmayer. On the 23rd of May, 2006, the Prosecution filed its submission of the expert report by Andreas Riedlmayer. The filing has been translated and was served on the accused on the 4th of October, 2006. According to Rule 94 bis, the accused has a 30-day time limit to file a notice indicating whether he accepts the expert report -- the expert witness report or if he wishes to cross-examine the witness, and if he challenges the qualifications of the witness as an expert or the relevance of the report. On the 22nd of November, 2006, the accused filed his response stating that he did not accept the expert report, that he wished to cross-examine the expert witness, and that he challenged the qualifications of the witness as an expert, and the relevance of the entire report. In addition, the accused requested additional time to file a notice under Rule 94 bis (B), since the report was provided to him on the 4th of October, 2006, during a time when counsel was assigned to him, and that this therefore made it unclear from when the 30-day limit should be calculated. The Chamber considers that the response provided by the accused is sufficient for the purpose of Rule 94 bis, under (B), as far as the non-acceptance of the report and the wish to cross-examine the witness are concerned, and therefore decides that the expert witness, Andreas Riedlmayer, shall be called for cross-examination. If any further submissions in writing are requested -- if the Defence would like to make any further submissions in writing in relation to the reasons why Mr. Riedlmayer does not qualify as an expert witness, the Defence will have 14 days from today to file any additional submissions. The next item on the agenda is the response to motions and new deadlines. There are a number of pending issues at this moment and new deadlines will need to be set for responses by the Defence now that counsel has been assigned. The Trial Chamber will issue a written decision in the next few days setting new deadlines for the Defence to respond to Prosecution motions. At this point, I'd like to ask the Defence to inform the Chamber, as soon as possible, if it would like the Trial Chamber to consider submissions made by them during the period of assigned counsel from the 21st of August to the 20th of October. Not necessarily to inform the Chamber today. But perhaps by tomorrow, Mr. Hooper, you could inform this Chamber. Then, finally, I come to one of the purposes of our Pre-Trial Conference, pursuant to Rule 73 bis, under (C). The Pre-Trial Judge, after having heard the Prosecutor, will determine, first, the number of witnesses the Prosecution may call, and, two, the time available to the Prosecutor for presenting evidence. As the parties were informed at the Rule 65 ter conference on the 20th of October, 2006, the Prosecution will be allowed to call 102 witnesses and will have 81.5 trial hours to present its case. I'm referring to the transcript of the Rule 65 ter conference of the 20th of October, page 22. The Chamber would like to know whether there are any other matters the parties would like to raise at this Pre-Trial Conference. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The first item relates to the witness order. I would like to make an oral request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have been informed that the witness -- that the Defence is not in a position to deal with the Witness VS-054 as planned to be the second witness, and has asked him to be moved back to next year. And to fill the court time most efficiently, we therefore would request to move forward the witnesses Paulic, Katic and Klajic. They were actually listed to testify in the period from the 13th to the -- the 13th to the 15th of December, but we think they can actually fill that slot for the Witness VS-054. We may be a bit too optimistic, because it may be that we are not as fast in the pace of this trial as we hope we will be. Therefore, the position is to have, after Mr. Balacevic, Ms. Paulic, Ms. Katic, and Ms. Klajic. However, what we need to keep at a particular day, that's the videolink, so that only those of -- of those three that I just mentioned would be called before the videolink. And also, we need to keep the Witness VS-017 in his position because he needs to be concluded. So we would only interpose those of the three that really fit before the videolink and before Witness VS-017.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would have a decision on this request by tomorrow, would that be timely enough, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, of course, before even considering to deliver decisions. Mr. Hooper, any submissions to be made in respect of the request just raised by Madam Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOOPER
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber will consider the matter and most likely will come with a decision tomorrow. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has one matter it would like to raise regarding Prosecution expert witness Ewa Tabeau. There is a -- at least a possibility that Dr. Tabeau could testify this year, by the 13th of December. And an issue has come up as to whether, if she does testify this year, the exact scope of her evidence. She has provided an expert report on the migration of non-Serbs from Hrtkovci, and that is why we have called Dr. Tabeau early in this case. However, she has also provided an extensive report regarding the migration of non-Serbs from certain municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And we communicated with the Defence on Friday and raised the issue of whether the Defence would be in a position to cross-examine Dr. Tabeau fully on all of her evidence should she be testifying on the 12th or perhaps the 13th of December. And we are still awaiting a response from the Defence on that. One option, obviously, would be to call Dr. Tabeau and have her testify about all of her expertise during one testimony. Another option might be to call Dr. Tabeau once regarding her expertise relating to Hrtkovci and to ask her to testify again in 2007 related to her expert report on Bosnia and Herzegovina. Another option also might be, that my colleague suggested to me today, is that all of her direct evidence could be provided this year on both of her expert reports; the cross-examination related to Bosnia and Herzegovina be held in abeyance until sometime next year. We simply want to present this issue to the Chamber now so it is aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the Defence already made up its mind in respect of this, or would you rather ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HOOPER
utterances.text: Well, there will be difficulties in respect of delving into reports that were not seen as relevant to this case until a few days ago. That's the problem that's posed. And the third option that's been suggested, that is, that all her evidence be given in chief and she be held back for cross-examination to a later time, certainly would seem an option, the favoured option.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could there be a possibility that the parties could exchange further views this afternoon and see whether they can agree on a certain course of action, and the Chamber will then consider whether it can follow the suggestions jointly made by the parties, if there would be any solution reached by them together. We'll then hear from you tomorrow, first of all, whether there is any agreed and favoured option; and second, if not, we'll further hear from the parties before determining the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other matter, madam Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there is one final matter, and that relates to a trial binder, map binder, for the trial. In the cases before this Tribunal, such binders are tendered in the very early stage of the proceedings. We actually have today here, in the courtroom, these trial binders with the maps that are of interest also already in the opening statement, and we wonder whether we should provide the trial binders now so that everyone can have it in front of them, not only on the screen. That's up to you. We have the trial binders for Your Honours, you Judges, and for the legal officers and also, of course, for the Defence. But we can hand it out today or a later date, whenever you like it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Hooper, that in anticipation of them being used, that they are already distributed?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOOPER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is my first e-court, and the start is now with a hard copy to start with. So then please distribute the hard copies of the map. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hooper, any other matter to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOOPER
utterances.text: I take it these don't come with magnifying glasses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think some of them are quite detailed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOOPER
utterances.text: Some are big enough to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Some are not. We'll see how they are used. That's one of the advantages, perhaps of e-court, that you can magnify matters on your screen. But I have not gone through it all. If there's no matter to be raised, then, we'll conclude this Pre-Trial Conference, and have a break of approximately half an hour. So we'll resume at 11.15 and then we'll have the start of the trial and, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, you're going to be invited to make your opening statement. This concludes the Pre-Trial Conference. We'll adjourn until quarter past 11.00.

procedural_notes.text: [Private session] [Confidentiality partially lifted by order of Trial Chamber]
